rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Single cell protein (SCP) ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Single cell protein (SCP)** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  **Single cell protein** is edible protein from microbes — bacteria, yeast, fungi, algae — grown on cheap substrates (whey, molasses, straw, even petroleum wastes). The name is a marketing choice: 'microbial protein' sounded unappetising. SCP can supply protein without farmland: a 250-kg cow gains ~200 g of protein per day; the same mass of microbes can produce tonnes of protein in hours.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Definition: protein from MICROBIAL biomass (Spirulina, Methylophilus methylotrophus, yeast, Chlorella) grown on waste — the microbe names are the marks.  ·  Trick 2: Merits: high protein (Spirulina >50%), fast growth (microbes double in hours), uses waste substrate, little land/water — four merits.

rows.text: **Worked example — the speed comparison.** A 250-kg cow adds about 200 g of protein per day. Microbial biomass doubling in ~2 hours means the same 250 kg of microbes, growing exponentially, can produce roughly 25 tonnes of protein in a single day (given substrate and oxygen).…  ·  ## 7.
